why: no model has been rendered and compared with the unit
claim: Type `01 61`'s mode byte picks a length, and the five it picks stand in the ratio 3 : 4 : 6 : 8 : 12 -- the ratio the single pitch shifter's five windows were measured to stand in. Read as the distance the output holds a copy of itself at, the five states give 28.50, 38.73, 57.90, 76.00, 114.02 ms, which against the first state is 1.000, 1.359, 2.031, 2.667, 4.001 where the ratio predicts 1, 1.333, 2, 2.667 and 4. Each distance is 0.891 to 0.908 of the window at the same state, a common multiple of 0.894 fitted over the differences leaving at most 0.81 ms of any of them, and that multiple is not explained here.
adds: This type carried no structural reading. It prints one shifter where the type beside it prints two and it prints a feedback byte that one does not, and the only claims naming it were the two that run across every type. What the window claim found was read off an artefact rate on one type; this is a distance in milliseconds on another, taken with a different stage, and it was predicted before the takes were made rather than read out of them.
refutedBy: A state of the mode byte whose distance is not the ratio the five lengths stand in, by more than the three sections put one state apart. The four lower states are bounded at 7.92 ms and the fifth is not bounded usefully at all, so a refutation would have to come from one of the four or from a run with more takes at the top.
whatItWouldChange: Rendering this type needs the same table of five lengths the type beside it needs, and not a second one read off its own page. The two print the same `1 - 5` against a byte with no unit beside it and the two answer to the same five ratios.

A byte printed as a bare count of states on this family has now been read as a length twice, on two types, by two quantities and two stages. The measurement that settles such a byte is a sweep of something else while the counted byte is held, and it is cheap.

alternatives.reading: The distance measured is the loop's, so what the mode byte moves is the feedback path rather than a read-out.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The copy is there with the feedback byte at the nought of its printed range. That section returns a distance at the same state and standing as far over the take with nothing in its path as the sections with the loop closed do, so what the output holds a copy of itself at does not need the loop to be there. It is the stage's own latency, and the loop adds further copies at multiples of it -- which is what the second peak of every reading here sits at.

alternatives.reading: The mode byte moves a length of its own that happens to fall near the ratio the other type's windows fall in.

separatedBy.observable: The same five distances with enough takes of each state that the ratio at the top of the byte is resolved.

predicts.the same five lengths: every state's ratio holds to the run's own repeats, including the fifth
predicts.a length of its own: at least one state departs by more than those repeats

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: The run's repeats are what bound this and they are not even across the byte: the three sections put the second state 1.46 ms apart and the fifth 25.02 ms apart. Twenty-five milliseconds on a state whose distance is 114 is twenty-two per cent, and the ratio being tested there is 4 against a measured 4.001 -- so the agreement at the top of the byte is inside the scatter and is not evidence. The four states under it are: the widest spread among them is 7.92 ms on a distance of 57.9.

run.settings: the five states, five takes of each
run.stimulus: the broadband program these takes were made on

alternatives.reading: The length the mode byte picks is proportional to the other type's window rather than being it.

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: A test on ratios cannot see a constant multiple, and the constant this run measured is 0.894 rather than one. What would separate them is where the latency sits inside the read-out, which is a place in a chain and not a quantity that leaves the unit.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: The reading is a ratio and the difference is a constant multiple, so this is recorded as equivalent rather than left open. Refusing to choose between two readings that both reproduce is the answer and not a deferral -- and the multiple itself is published so that a reader who has a use for it is not told it was one.
